analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Benchmarking GS macro views vs. market pricing for 2027
key_insights: GS economists expect 2027 global real GDP growth of 2.8%, slightly above 2.7% in 2026, with risks tilted to the downside. Lower energy prices and still-strong AI capex are expected to outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.

GS expects inflation to slow in 2027 as the impulse from US tariffs, energy and AI-related pressures fades. This supports only incremental policy tightening through early 2027 in most major economies, followed by gradual normalization cuts later in 2027.

Markets have already repriced growth lower over the past few months. The RAI PC1 global growth factor fell as cyclicals sold off against defensives, equities underperformed bonds and credit spreads widened. Growth pricing showed some strength last week.

The valuation reset in risky assets and a Risk Appetite Indicator still close to 0 suggest a lower bar for risky assets to deliver positive returns if growth stays healthy next year. Both upside and downside tails remain possible.
GS baseline policy forecasts are more dovish than market pricing for 2027. The gap is widest for the ECB (normalisation cuts from 2027Q4), then the Fed, SNB and BoE, and narrowest for the BoJ.

GS economists expect two 25bp Fed hikes in Dec. 2026 and March 2027, followed by gradual cuts starting in Nov. 2027. They expect only one BoE hike, in February, and three 25bp BoJ hikes in Dec. 2026, March 2027 and June 2027.
GS rates forecasts sit below market pricing, most of all for UK and US 2y yields. The rates team expects the largest 10y bond rallies in the US and UK, and the most 2s10s Gilt curve steepening.

On a risk-adjusted basis, GS forecasts differ most from market pricing for CNY and BRL. FX strategists expect further CNY strength from strong exports, persistent undervaluation and policy support for gradual appreciation. BRL and COP are seen supported by high carry and tight monetary policy in a more range-bound dollar backdrop.

GS strategists see the most upside relative to market pricing in US, EM and Japan equities, driven by slowing but healthy earnings growth. The 12m S&P 500 forecast is 8700 against a current 7562. Topix is forecast at 4500 against 3942.

In commodities, strategists see the largest upside versus futures in copper (AI and electrification demand meeting constrained supply) and gold (structural central-bank buying and eventual Fed easing). The 12m gold forecast is $4,610/oz and copper $15,600/mt, while Brent is forecast at $80 and WTI at $72.
GS economists name three main risks to steady growth: higher energy prices from a renewed escalation in Iran, fiscal risks raising long-term yields, and disappointments in AI capex growth.

Since October markets have become more worried about AI capex, with a rising implied probability of a further semiconductor sell-off. The implied probability of a further sell-off in long-dated USTs has eased. The probability of a further rise in oil prices is flat and below the March peak.

Asset allocation stance: overweight equities (US, Japan), underweight Stoxx 600, neutral Asia-Pacific ex Japan, underweight corporate bonds, neutral commodities except overweight gold, and overweight cash at 3m moving to neutral at 12m. For 10y government bonds the stance is neutral at 3m and overweight at 12m, with US, Germany and UK overweight or neutral by tenor.

charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows markets have repriced growth lower, with the RAI PC1 global growth factor falling as cyclicals sold off relative to defensives, equities underperformed bonds and credit spreads widened.
Exhibit 2 compares YE27 vs. YE26 policy rates for GS baseline and market pricing, with the gap widest for the ECB and narrowest for the BoJ.
Exhibit 3 compares GS 12m forecasts across asset classes to market pricing, divided by each asset's implied volatility, with CNY and BRL the largest differences.
Exhibit 4 shows market-implied 3m probabilities of oil up more than 25%, 20Y+ USTs down more than 5% and semiconductors down more than 20%.
vol_and_positioning: Market-implied probabilities of semiconductor stocks falling more than 20% over 3 months have risen since October. The implied probability of 20Y+ USTs falling more than 5% has eased. The probability of oil rising more than 25% is flat and below the March peak.
The Risk Appetite Indicator is still close to 0. Cyclicals sold off relative to defensives, equities underperformed bonds and credit spreads widened over recent months.
3m ATM implied volatility is 14.7 for the S&P 500 (51st percentile), 14.9 for Euro Stoxx 50, 27.5 for the Nikkei 225 (94th percentile) and 26.1 for MSCI EM (92nd percentile).

1m realised volatility is 22.3 for the S&P 500 (85th percentile), 36.5 for the Nikkei 225 (95th percentile) and 22.5 for MSCI EM (89th percentile), above their 3m implied levels for the S&P 500 and Nikkei.
S&P 500 12m forward P/E is 18.2x (41st percentile of the last 10 years, 10y average 19.2x). Stoxx 600 is 14.1x (49th percentile). US IG spread is 86bp and US HY spread is 316bp.
geopolitical: Renewed escalation in Iran is named as a risk that would lift energy prices and threaten the baseline view of steady growth.
The impulse from US tariffs is expected to fade in 2027, contributing to slowing inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: GS economists expect 2.8% global growth in 2027 as lower energy prices and still-strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. With the Risk Appetite Indicator near 0 and valuations reset, the bar for risky assets is lower.
tension_points.bear_case: Three risks threaten the baseline: higher energy prices from a renewed Iran escalation, fiscal risks lifting long-term yields, and disappointing AI capex growth. Markets have already repriced growth lower and worry more about AI capex since October.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No level is stated. The report tracks 3m market-implied probabilities of oil up more than 25%, 20Y+ USTs down more than 5% and semiconductors down more than 20% (Exhibit 4) as the tails that would break the baseline.

tension_points.theme: GS policy path vs market pricing
tension_points.bull_case: GS economists see only incremental tightening through early 2027 followed by gradual cuts as inflation falls, so rates should rally more than priced, notably in US and UK 10y yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Market pricing embeds a more hawkish path than GS for the ECB, Fed, SNB and BoE. Fiscal risks raising long-term yields are a named risk to the GS rates view.
